capabilities.target: vendor master record, including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The agent is told to update the vendor's bank record whenever 'the invoice shows new bank details', with no independent verification channel specified. This accepts the single most attacker-controlled field (payment destination) on the authority of the invoice content alone.

The only named safeguard for an irreversible payment or a bank-detail change is a prompt instruction to request approval with a model-written one-line summary. Nothing in the instructions requires the summary to disclose that bank details changed.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by a human reviewer, which is structural, but the reviewer sees only the model's one-line summary rather than the raw action (approval_review_mode: model_summary). The observed example card does not disclose that bank details changed. A more capable or more persuasive model can write a summary that is accurate about the payment while omitting the riskiest fact (ASI09). Fails under model_upgrade, autonomy_increase, and control_removal.

controls.name: Out-of-band vendor callback verification for bank-detail changes
controls.decay_rationale: Would verify any bank-detail change via a phone call to a number already on file, independent of model output and independent of the approval summary. Does not decay with model capability because it does not depend on what the model reports.

controls.name: Raw-action approval review showing bank-detail diff
controls.decay_rationale: Would show the approver the actual old versus new bank account and routing numbers and change history pulled from the system of record, rather than a model-written summary, removing the ASI09 dependency on the model's disclosure choices.

controls.name: Segregated least-privilege ERP roles (maker-checker)
controls.decay_rationale: Would replace the single broad ERP credential (currently able to update any vendor and schedule any payment) with separate least-privilege roles for read-matching, bank updates, and payment scheduling, limiting blast radius regardless of model behavior.

findings.title: TC4/TC9: Unverified invoice-driven bank-detail change plus summary-gated approval enables payment redirection fraud

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled or spoofed invoice uploaded to the supplier portal claims new bank details for a known vendor
Agent reads the vendor master record to match the invoice to a vendor and purchase order
Agent updates the vendor's bank details directly from invoice content
The one-line summary card observed in evidence lists only payee, amount, invoice number, and PO match, with no indication that bank details were just changed
Agent schedules an irreversible payment to the newly updated, attacker-controlled bank account

findings.residual_rationale: Crediting ctl.clerk_approval as a model_summary human approval gate alone would float residual to the rubric floor of moderate (-2 tiers from critical). But the approval card artifact itself shows the one-line summary discloses only payee, amount, invoice number, and PO match, and never states that a bank-detail change occurred on this vendor. The gate therefore provides essentially no check on the single riskiest element of the path (the bank account change) even though it formally covers cap.bank_update. This disclosure gap is a present design fact the model_summary classification does not fully capture, so residual is rated high rather than moderate.

forecast.watch_signal: Platform or model version string changes with no separate review (subject.model.swappable is true); approval volume per clerk rising further above the current ~150 cards/day; any change that narrows, batches, or removes the clerk_approval step.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to update the vendor record whenever 'the invoice shows new bank details', with no independent verification step named.
The only control named for payment or bank changes is a model-generated one-line approval summary.
The example card shows only payee, amount, invoice number, and PO match; it does not state that a bank-detail change occurred.
'The card shows only the model's summary. Bank account numbers and the change history are not shown.'
'The ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment' confirms one broad, non-least-privilege credential spans both sensitive actions.
'The model is upgraded with the platform, with no separate review' confirms the model_upgrade trigger applies with no compensating review step.

recommendations.action: Change the approval card to a raw-action review: show old versus new bank account and routing numbers and an explicit 'BANK DETAILS CHANGED' flag whenever a bank update is part of the transaction being approved.

Require out-of-band verification (a callback to a phone number already on file, not one taken from the invoice) before any vendor bank-detail change is applied, independent of the model and the approval summary.

Split the single broad ERP credential into least-privilege, maker-checker roles: one for vendor and invoice read-matching, a separately controlled role for bank-detail updates, and a separate role for payment scheduling.
Treat any model or platform upgrade as a significant change requiring reassessment of the clerk_approval gate, since subject.model is currently swappable with no separate review.
Monitor clerk approval throughput and approval rate for signs of approval fatigue (currently about 150 cards per day); sample-audit approved bank-detail changes weekly.

rating.rationale: There is one material path: an untrusted, externally authored supplier invoice can drive both an irreversible vendor bank-detail change and an irreversible outbound payment (S3 sinks), both reachable under a single broad ERP credential. Inherent risk is critical (U source to S3 sink). The only preventive control is a clerk approval gated on a model-written one-line summary; the approval card evidence shows that summary does not even disclose that a bank change occurred, so residual is rated high rather than the generic moderate floor a model_summary gate would otherwise earn. The subject's model is declared swappable with no separate review, so a routine model upgrade (or an autonomy increase or control removal) is expected to defeat the summary-gated approval entirely, returning the design to its critical inherent risk. The structural fixes that would actually sever the path -- out-of-band vendor verification and a raw-action approval review -- are both currently absent.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration shown in the provided artifacts (system prompt, one example approval card, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent over time.

No MCP config, tool manifest, or IaC was provided; credential_scope and data_sensitivity for the ERP capabilities are inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on the exact permission boundaries of the ERP credential is medium.
max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes were not specified in any artifact and were treated as null/unknown for the autonomy modifier check.

Only one example approval card was provided; whether every bank-detail change is always summarized this way, or whether some cards do disclose the change, could not be confirmed and would require the actual card-generation logic or a larger sample of cards.
